concepts.primary_objective: Create a pie chart in a spreadsheet to show part-to-whole composition.
concepts.assessment_target: Given category totals that sum to a meaningful whole, build a correctly-encoded pie chart showing each category's share.
concepts.practice_objective: Build a pie chart showing each product category's share of total revenue.
concepts.central_mental_model: A pie chart encodes each category's share of a single meaningful total as a proportional wedge of a circle.

concepts.concept_name: matplotlib figure and axes object model

toc_location.tile_summary: Create a figure and axes, control layout and size, and plot with pyplot.

concepts.primary_objective: Understand matplotlib's Figure/Axes object model as the container/canvas relationship underlying every plot.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a plotting task, correctly identify which calls create the Figure vs. the Axes and where plotted elements attach.
concepts.practice_objective: Create a Figure with one Axes explicitly and plot a simple line on that Axes object.
concepts.central_mental_model: A Figure is the overall canvas/window, and an Axes is one plotting area within it that actual plot calls draw onto.

toc_location.tile_summary: Create a figure and axes, control layout and size, and plot with pyplot.

concepts.primary_objective: Adjust a matplotlib figure's size and layout so a plot renders clearly.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a plot with cramped or oddly-proportioned output, adjust figure size/layout so it renders clearly.
concepts.practice_objective: Resize a figure and use tight_layout to fix overlapping axis labels.
concepts.central_mental_model: Figure size and layout settings control the canvas dimensions and spacing independent of what data is being plotted.

concepts.concept_name: Basic plot creation with the pyplot interface

toc_location.tile_summary: Create a figure and axes, control layout and size, and plot with pyplot.

concepts.primary_objective: Create a basic plot using matplotlib's pyplot interface.
concepts.assessment_target: Given data and a plot requirement, produce a correct basic plot using pyplot's plotting functions.
concepts.practice_objective: Plot a simple line chart of one numeric series using plt.plot().
concepts.central_mental_model: pyplot provides a stateful, quick-plotting interface where each call implicitly acts on 'the current' figure and axes.

toc_location.tile_summary: Compare categories with bar charts and show distributions with histograms.

concepts.primary_objective: Create a bar chart to compare a numeric value across discrete categories.
concepts.assessment_target: Given categorical summary data, build a bar chart that correctly compares the categories.
concepts.practice_objective: Plot a bar chart comparing average value across categories.
concepts.central_mental_model: A bar chart encodes a value as bar length/height, suited to comparing discrete categories.

toc_location.tile_summary: Compare categories with bar charts and show distributions with histograms.

concepts.primary_objective: Create a histogram to visualize the distribution of a single numeric variable.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a numeric column, build a histogram with a reasonable bin count that reveals its distribution shape.
concepts.practice_objective: Plot a histogram of a numeric column and adjust the bin count to better reveal its shape.
concepts.central_mental_model: A histogram bins a continuous variable into ranges and shows frequency as bar height, revealing distribution shape.

toc_location.tile_summary: Show trends with line plots, relationships with scatter plots, and spread with box plots.

concepts.primary_objective: Create a line plot to visualize a trend over an ordered sequence such as time.
concepts.assessment_target: Given time-ordered numeric data, build a line plot that shows the trend correctly.
concepts.practice_objective: Plot a line chart of a numeric value over time.
concepts.central_mental_model: A line plot connects ordered points to make a trend's direction and rate of change visible.

toc_location.tile_summary: Show trends with line plots, relationships with scatter plots, and spread with box plots.

concepts.primary_objective: Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between two numeric variables.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two related numeric columns, build a scatter plot that reveals their relationship.
concepts.practice_objective: Plot a scatter plot of two numeric columns and describe the apparent relationship.
concepts.central_mental_model: A scatter plot places one point per row at (x, y), revealing correlation or clustering between two numeric variables.

toc_location.tile_summary: Show trends with line plots, relationships with scatter plots, and spread with box plots.

concepts.primary_objective: Create a box plot to visualize a numeric variable's spread and outliers, optionally across groups.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a numeric column (optionally grouped), build a box plot that correctly shows its quartiles and outliers.
concepts.practice_objective: Plot a box plot comparing a numeric column's distribution across several categories.
concepts.central_mental_model: A box plot summarizes a distribution's quartiles, median, and outliers as one compact shape, and does so per group when grouped.

toc_location.tile_summary: Label and annotate a chart, then choose the right chart type for a given question.

concepts.primary_objective: Add titles, axis labels, and legends to a plot for readability.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an unlabeled plot, add the correct title, axis labels, and legend so it is understandable on its own.
concepts.practice_objective: Add a title, both axis labels, and a legend distinguishing two plotted series.
concepts.central_mental_model: Labeling attaches human-readable text (title, axis labels, legend) onto a plot that already correctly shows the data.

concepts.concept_name: Matching chart type to the analytical question

toc_location.tile_summary: Label and annotate a chart, then choose the right chart type for a given question.

concepts.primary_objective: Match a chart type to the analytical question being explored (comparison, trend, distribution, relationship).
concepts.assessment_target: Given an analytical question, choose the chart type best suited to answering it during exploratory analysis.
concepts.practice_objective: Given a dataset and an analytical question, justify choosing a scatter plot instead of a bar chart.
concepts.central_mental_model: Different chart types encode data differently, so the right one to use for one's own exploration depends on the shape of the analytical question being asked, not on personal preference.

concepts.concept_name: Plotting directly from pandas DataFrames with seaborn

toc_location.tile_summary: Plot DataFrames with seaborn, use its statistical plotting functions, and apply themes and palettes.

concepts.primary_objective: Plot directly from a pandas DataFrame's columns using seaborn's data= and column-name arguments.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a DataFrame, build a seaborn plot by passing the DataFrame and column names directly, rather than extracting arrays first.
concepts.practice_objective: Plot a seaborn bar chart directly from a DataFrame using data= and x=/y= column names.
concepts.central_mental_model: Seaborn functions accept a DataFrame plus column names directly, letting the plot reference columns by name instead of manually extracting each array.

toc_location.tile_summary: Plot DataFrames with seaborn, use its statistical plotting functions, and apply themes and palettes.

concepts.primary_objective: Visualize statistical relationships and distributions using seaborn's dedicated statistical plotting functions.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a statistical relationship/distribution question, use the correct seaborn statistical function to visualize it directly.
concepts.practice_objective: Use a seaborn statistical plotting function to visualize the relationship between two numeric variables with a fitted trend.
concepts.central_mental_model: Seaborn's statistical functions compute and draw a statistical summary (e.g. a regression fit or distribution estimate) as part of plotting, beyond matplotlib's raw plotting.

concepts.concept_name: seaborn built-in themes and color palettes

toc_location.tile_summary: Plot DataFrames with seaborn, use its statistical plotting functions, and apply themes and palettes.

concepts.primary_objective: Apply seaborn's built-in themes and color palettes to a plot.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a plot needing a consistent, polished look, apply a seaborn theme and palette correctly.
concepts.practice_objective: Apply a seaborn theme and a categorical color palette to an existing plot.
concepts.central_mental_model: A seaborn theme sets global plot styling (background, gridlines, fonts) and a palette sets the color set used for categories, independent of what's being plotted.

toc_location.tile_summary: Customize a chart's visual style and lay out multiple plots in one figure.

concepts.primary_objective: Apply custom styling/theming to matplotlib/seaborn plots beyond the built-in defaults.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a branding or presentation requirement, apply custom style settings (colors, fonts, style sheets) to a plot.
concepts.practice_objective: Apply a custom color palette and font size setting to a plot's style beyond seaborn's built-in themes.
concepts.central_mental_model: Custom styling overrides matplotlib/seaborn's default appearance settings globally or per plot, layered on top of whatever chart type and data are already correct.

toc_location.tile_summary: Customize a chart's visual style and lay out multiple plots in one figure.

concepts.primary_objective: Lay out multiple related plots in one figure using subplots.
concepts.assessment_target: Given several related plots, arrange them into one multi-panel figure with the correct grid layout.
concepts.practice_objective: Create a 2x2 grid of subplots each showing a different numeric column's histogram.
concepts.central_mental_model: Subplots divide one figure into a grid of independent Axes, letting several related plots share one figure.

concepts.concept_name: Basic A/B test structure (control vs treatment group)

toc_location.tile_summary: Understand how an A/B test is structured and interpret the lift between variants.

concepts.primary_objective: Understand the basic structure of an A/B test: a control group and a treatment group.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an experiment description, correctly identify its control and treatment groups and what's being compared.
concepts.practice_objective: Given an A/B test description, identify the control group, the treatment group, and the metric being compared.
concepts.central_mental_model: An A/B test compares an unchanged control group against a treatment group that received the change, isolating the change's effect by holding everything else equal.

toc_location.tile_summary: Understand how an A/B test is structured and interpret the lift between variants.

concepts.primary_objective: Interpret lift/percentage change between two groups' results.
concepts.assessment_target: Given control and treatment results, compute and correctly interpret the lift/percentage change between them.
concepts.practice_objective: Given a control conversion rate and a treatment conversion rate, compute and interpret the lift.
concepts.central_mental_model: Lift expresses a treatment group's result relative to the control group's, as a percentage change, answering 'how much better/worse'.

concepts.concept_name: Conceptual effect of sample size on confidence

toc_location.tile_title: Sample Size, Significance, and Business Conclusions
toc_location.tile_summary: Understand how sample size affects results, interpret statistical significance and confidence, and draw a business conclusion from an experiment.

concepts.primary_objective: Conceptually understand how sample size affects confidence in a result.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two experiments differing only in sample size, correctly explain which result should be trusted more and why.
concepts.practice_objective: Given two A/B tests with the same lift but different sample sizes, explain which result is more trustworthy.
concepts.central_mental_model: A larger sample size generally produces a more reliable estimate, because random noise averages out more as more observations are included.

concepts.concept_name: Conceptual interpretation of statistical significance/confidence level

toc_location.tile_title: Sample Size, Significance, and Business Conclusions
toc_location.tile_summary: Understand how sample size affects results, interpret statistical significance and confidence, and draw a business conclusion from an experiment.

concepts.primary_objective: Conceptually interpret statistical significance and confidence level in an experiment result.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an experiment result reported with a significance/confidence figure, correctly explain what that figure does and doesn't tell you about the result.
concepts.practice_objective: Given a result reported as 'significant at 95% confidence', explain in plain language what that claim does and doesn't mean.
concepts.central_mental_model: Confidence level and statistical significance are two framings of the same idea: how unlikely the observed result would be if there were truly no effect — interpreted conceptually here, not derived mathematically.

concepts.concept_name: Drawing a business conclusion from an experiment-result summary

toc_location.tile_title: Sample Size, Significance, and Business Conclusions
toc_location.tile_summary: Understand how sample size affects results, interpret statistical significance and confidence, and draw a business conclusion from an experiment.

concepts.primary_objective: Draw a business conclusion from an experiment-result summary.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an experiment's results, state a correct business conclusion that follows from the data without overreaching.
concepts.practice_objective: Given an A/B test summary, write the business conclusion a stakeholder should act on.
concepts.central_mental_model: A business conclusion translates a statistical result into a decision-relevant statement, going one step beyond simply reporting the numbers.

concepts.concept_name: Identifying the business decision a stakeholder needs the analysis to inform

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify the decision behind a request, state findings precisely, frame the analytical question, and identify stakeholder requirements.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify the business decision a stakeholder needs an analysis to inform.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a stakeholder request, correctly identify the underlying decision the analysis is meant to support.
concepts.practice_objective: Given a vague stakeholder request, state the specific decision it's meant to inform.
concepts.central_mental_model: Every analysis request exists to inform some decision; naming that decision up front focuses everything that follows.

concepts.concept_name: Stating a finding precisely and quantitatively (the specific number or comparison, not a vague claim)

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify the decision behind a request, state findings precisely, frame the analytical question, and identify stakeholder requirements.

concepts.primary_objective: State a finding precisely and quantitatively, with the specific number or comparison rather than a vague claim.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an analysis result, state the finding using the specific number/comparison rather than a vague qualitative claim.
concepts.practice_objective: Rewrite the vague finding 'sales went up' as a precise, quantified statement.
concepts.central_mental_model: A precise finding names the actual number or comparison, letting a reader verify the claim, unlike a vague qualitative statement.

concepts.concept_name: Converting a vague business question into a specific, measurable analytical question

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify the decision behind a request, state findings precisely, frame the analytical question, and identify stakeholder requirements.

concepts.primary_objective: Convert a vague business question into a specific, measurable analytical question.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a vague business question, restate it as a specific, measurable analytical question that can actually be answered with data.
concepts.practice_objective: Turn the vague question 'are we doing well?' into a specific, measurable analytical question.
concepts.central_mental_model: A measurable analytical question names a specific metric, comparison, and timeframe, unlike a vague business question that can't be directly answered.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify the decision behind a request, state findings precisely, frame the analytical question, and identify stakeholder requirements.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify a stakeholder's actual requirements before starting an analysis.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a stakeholder conversation or request, correctly identify what data, scope, and output the analysis actually requires.
concepts.practice_objective: Given a stakeholder's request, list the requirements (data needed, scope, deadline, output format) before starting.
concepts.central_mental_model: Requirements gathering surfaces what's actually needed (data, scope, format, timing) before analysis work begins, preventing rework later.

toc_location.tile_summary: Turn a finding into a data-driven recommendation and translate technical results into plain language.

concepts.primary_objective: Make a recommendation that is explicitly grounded in the analysis's data and findings.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an analysis's findings, write a recommendation that is clearly and correctly grounded in that specific data.
concepts.practice_objective: Given a set of findings, write a recommendation and explicitly cite which finding justifies it.
concepts.central_mental_model: A data-driven recommendation is explicitly traceable back to the specific finding(s) that justify it, not a generic best practice.

concepts.concept_name: Translating technical results into plain-language takeaways

toc_location.tile_summary: Turn a finding into a data-driven recommendation and translate technical results into plain language.

concepts.primary_objective: Translate technical results into plain-language takeaways for a non-technical audience.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a technical result, restate it in plain language a non-technical stakeholder can immediately understand.
concepts.practice_objective: Rewrite a technically-worded statistical result as a one-sentence plain-language takeaway.
concepts.central_mental_model: Plain-language translation keeps the finding's substance while removing jargon the audience isn't equipped to parse.

concepts.concept_name: Prioritizing findings by relevance to the stakeholder's specific decision, not by analytical interestingness

toc_location.tile_summary: Prioritize which findings matter most, frame recommendations as clear actions, and set up narrative context.

concepts.primary_objective: Prioritize findings by relevance to the stakeholder's specific decision, not by analytical interestingness.
concepts.assessment_target: Given several findings, correctly rank which to lead with based on relevance to the stakeholder's decision, not analytical novelty.
concepts.practice_objective: Given five findings, choose and justify which two to lead a stakeholder summary with.
concepts.central_mental_model: Prioritizing by decision-relevance means the most statistically interesting finding is not automatically the one to lead with.

concepts.concept_name: Framing an actionable recommendation that is distinct from the finding itself

toc_location.tile_summary: Prioritize which findings matter most, frame recommendations as clear actions, and set up narrative context.

concepts.primary_objective: Frame an actionable recommendation that is distinct from the finding itself.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a finding, write a recommendation stating what action should be taken, distinct from restating the finding.
concepts.practice_objective: Given the finding 'churn is highest in the first 30 days', write a distinct, actionable recommendation.
concepts.central_mental_model: A recommendation proposes what to do about a finding; simply restating the finding again is not a recommendation.

concepts.concept_name: Writing the context/setup for a findings narrative (why this analysis, what question it answers)

toc_location.tile_summary: Prioritize which findings matter most, frame recommendations as clear actions, and set up narrative context.

concepts.primary_objective: Write the context/setup for a findings narrative explaining why the analysis was done and what question it answers.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a finished analysis, write an opening context section that states why it was done and what question it answers.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a two-sentence context section introducing a findings report's purpose and question.
concepts.central_mental_model: A narrative's context/setup orients the reader before any finding is presented, answering 'why am I reading this' first.

concepts.concept_name: Tailoring level of detail to audience technical background

toc_location.tile_summary: Tailor the level of detail to the audience and anticipate the questions or objections they'll raise.

concepts.primary_objective: Tailor the level of technical detail in a presentation to the audience's technical background.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two different audiences for the same analysis, correctly adjust the level of technical detail for each.
concepts.practice_objective: Rewrite the same finding at two different technical-detail levels for two different audiences.
concepts.central_mental_model: Tailoring detail means the same underlying finding is presented with more or less technical depth depending on who's receiving it, without changing its substance.

toc_location.tile_summary: Tailor the level of detail to the audience and anticipate the questions or objections they'll raise.

concepts.primary_objective: Anticipate the questions and objections a stakeholder is likely to raise about a finding or recommendation.

concepts.practice_objective: Given a recommendation, list two likely stakeholder objections and how you'd respond to each.
concepts.central_mental_model: Anticipating objections means thinking from the audience's incentives and concerns, not just re-checking your own analysis.

concepts.concept_name: Matching chart type to the specific point being made (trend vs. comparison vs. distribution vs. part-to-whole)

concepts.practice_objective: Given the point 'this category dominates the total', choose and justify a chart type that makes that point clearly to a stakeholder.
concepts.central_mental_model: Choosing a chart type here is about which chart most clearly conveys an already-found point to an audience, distinct from choosing a chart type to explore data during one's own analysis.

concepts.concept_name: Simplifying a technical chart for a non-technical audience (removing gridlines, axis clutter, unneeded precision)

toc_location.tile_title: Matching and Simplifying Charts for an Audience
toc_location.tile_summary: Match a chart type to the point you're making and simplify it for a non-technical audience.

concepts.primary_objective: Simplify a technical chart for a non-technical audience by removing gridlines, axis clutter, and unneeded precision.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a technical-looking chart, simplify it for a non-technical audience while preserving its accuracy.
concepts.practice_objective: Take an over-detailed chart and simplify it by removing gridlines, excess decimal precision, and axis clutter.
concepts.central_mental_model: Simplifying for an audience means removing visual elements that serve the analyst but distract a non-technical viewer, without changing the underlying data or claim.
